answer: The network can run sting offers: undercover protocol accounts quietly post bribes asking graders to vote in a bloc or rent out their keys. Any identity that accepts, or answers through a shared coordinator, has its stake slashed and is linked to every account that took the same lure. Honest agents simply ignore the bait, but a sybil farm lives on coordination, so it keeps stepping into traps. Like thin ice over a tundra river, nobody knows which offer is fake, and the risk on the horizon makes renting votes a losing bet.
